hypothesis: The only prior distinct T1 candidate (d35c915c07694ddb) was valid at 4.42078e-05 seconds over three samples, versus the baseline's 4.64832e-05 seconds over three samples; these whole-call results do not isolate the cause. That candidate finalized up to 1024 partials in one CTA. This variant keeps the 128-thread reduction tree and 128-input first-stage tile fixed, but lowers the finalizer cap to 256. It tests whether parallelizing intermediate counts such as 512 partials offsets the added launch. At n=4,194,304, the expected hierarchy still reduces 32,768 initial partials to 256 before finalization. No speedup is assumed.
notes: The prior catalog had one distinct T1 program and one valid measured trial, with no observed duplicate. This candidate changes the finalizer threshold rather than renaming that program. Partial sums remain int64 through finalization, and scratch stages alternate between two packed buffers, reading only elements written by earlier kernels. This candidate has not been measured; the controller should validate it and collect repeated full-call timings. No failed variant is present in the supplied observations.
transformations: Kept the 128-thread modulo/shared-memory reduction tree for the input partial kernel and all parallel partial-reduction stages.
Accumulate input and intermediate partials as int64; narrow only when the exact total is written to the int output.
Lowered the one-CTA finalization cap to 256 partials; counts above the cap go through parallel 128-way reduction stages.
Use two packed scratch buffers sized by the initial partial count, alternate stage outputs, and write the final result directly to out.
Handle n == 0 as a zero sum and reject invalid n or required null pointers without relying on scratch initialization.
